source.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφ’ ὃν οὐδεὶς οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν· λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε.

records.literal_gloss: And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of the Olives, he sends two of the disciples of him \v 2 and says to them, Go into the village the [one] opposite you, and immediately entering into it you will find a colt having been tied on which no one yet of men has sat; untie it and bring [it].

en.L: And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples \v 2 and says to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and immediately as you enter it you will find a colt tied, on which no one among {{gender:people|men}} has yet sat; untie it and bring [it].
en.B: As they were approaching Jerusalem and came near Bethphage and Bethany, by the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent off two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples \v 2 with these instructions: "Go to the village ahead of you. The moment you go in, you will find a colt tied up there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were getting close to Jerusalem. They came near the towns of Bethphage and Bethany, close to the Mount of Olives. Then Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples ahead. \v 2 He told them, "Go into the village in front of you. As soon as you get there, you will find a young donkey tied up. No one has ever ridden it. Untie it and bring it to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y cuando se acercan a Jerusalén, a Betfagé y a Betania, junto al monte de los Olivos, envía a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos \v 2 y les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea que está frente a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y en cuanto {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en ella {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} un pollino atado, sobre el cual todavía no se ha sentado {{gender:ninguna persona|ningún hombre}}; {{plural_you:desátenlo|desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganlo|traedlo}}.
es.B: Cuando ya se acercaban a Jerusalén, cerca de Betfagé y Betania, junto al monte de los Olivos, Jesús envió a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos \v 2 con este encargo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} delante. En cuanto {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} allí atado un pollino que nadie ha montado nunca. {{plural_you:Desátenlo|Desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganlo|traedlo}} aquí.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se estaban acercando a Jerusalén. Llegaron cerca de los pueblos de Betfagé y Betania, junto al monte de los Olivos. Entonces Jesús mandó por delante a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. \v 2 Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al pueblo que está ahí delante. En cuanto {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}}, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} un burrito atado. Nadie lo ha montado nunca. {{plural_you:Desátenlo|Desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganmelo|traédmelo}}.

sw.L: Na wanapokaribia Yerusalemu, kwenye Bethfage na Bethania, karibu na Mlima wa Mizeituni, anawatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} \v 2 na kuwaambia, "Nendeni kijijini kilicho mkabala nanyi, na papo hapo mkiingia humo mtamkuta mwana-punda amefungwa, ambaye juu yake hajaketi mtu yeyote bado; mfungueni na mleteni.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakikaribia Yerusalemu, wakafika karibu na Bethfage na Bethania, kando ya Mlima wa Mizeituni, Yesu aliwatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} \v 2 akiwapa maagizo haya: "Nendeni kwenye kijiji kilicho mkabala nanyi. Punde mtakapoingia humo, mtakuta mwana-punda amefungwa, ambaye hakuna mtu aliyewahi kumpanda. Mfungueni, mumlete hapa.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wanakaribia Yerusalemu. Walifika karibu na vijiji vya Bethfage na Bethania, vilivyo kando ya Mlima wa Mizeituni. Kisha Yesu akawatuma wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawili watangulie. \v 2 Akawaambia, "Nendeni katika kijiji kilicho mbele yenu. Mara tu mtakapofika huko, mtamkuta punda mchanga amefungwa. Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kumpanda. Mfungueni, mumlete {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.

decisions.choice: draw near, sends, says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they came near, and he sent two disciples and told them.

decisions.choice: Bethphage and Bethany: villages on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives, across a valley east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Bethany lay about fifteen stadia, a little under two miles, from Jerusalem (John 11:18). Travelers coming up from Jericho (10:46) reached these villages before crossing the Mount of Olives to the city.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the place where Zechariah saw the Lord come to stand on the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 says the Lord's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives. Mark names the hill as Jesus comes to Jerusalem, and it returns in 13:3 and 14:26.

decisions.choice: colt: a young animal, here a young donkey
decisions.reason: The word means the young of an animal and could be used of horses. Matthew 21:2 and John 12:14-15 make it a donkey, and the scene echoes Zechariah 9:9, where Zion's king comes riding on a donkey's colt.

decisions.choice: on which no one has yet sat: an animal not yet put to ordinary use
decisions.reason: Animals set apart for sacred use had never borne a yoke (Numbers 19:2; Deuteronomy 21:3; 1 Samuel 6:7). The unridden colt fits a king's first entry into his city.

decisions.choice: a young donkey; bring it to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of animal is meant and where to bring it. Literal and Balanced keep "colt".

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (se acercan, envía, dice); past at Balanced and Readable (se acercaban, envió, dijo)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 4, 7, 15, 21, 22, 27 and 33.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives ({{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}); none on tráiganmelo (R) or on verbs with no subject pronoun
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("envía", "dijo") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("tráiganmelo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanapokaribia, anawatuma); past at Balanced and Readable (walipokuwa wakikaribia, aliwatuma)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 4, 7, 15, 21, 22, 27 and 33.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on free pronouns and possessives only ({{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}})
decisions.reason: The English "he" and "him" take the setting. Swahili carries them in the verb's prefixes (anawatuma, walimjia), which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο;

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone to you says, Why are you doing this?

en.L: And if anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?'
en.B: Should anyone ask you, 'Why are you doing this?'
en.R: Someone may ask you, 'Why are you doing that?'

es.L: Y si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} dice: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto?”,
es.B: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto?”,
es.R: Puede que alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunte: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} eso?”.

sw.L: Na kama mtu yeyote akiwaambia, 'Kwa nini mnafanya hivi?'
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akiwauliza, 'Kwa nini mnafanya hivyo?'
sw.R: Huenda mtu akawauliza, 'Kwa nini mnafanya hivyo?'

decisions.choice: if anyone says to you: Jesus prepares them for a challenge he expects
decisions.reason: Jesus knows that taking an animal will be questioned, and it is (11:5). His words are fulfilled as he spoke them (11:6).

decisions.choice: Someone may ask you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the condition into a short sentence of its own; the next sentence gives the answer.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" ({{plural_you:les|os}}, {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} and onward)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: εἴπατε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει· καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει πάλιν ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: say, The Lord of it need has, and immediately it he sends back here.

en.L: say, 'The Lord has need of it, and immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends it back here.'"
en.B: tell them, 'The Lord needs it, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send it back here without delay.'"
en.R: tell them, 'The Lord needs it. He will send it back here soon.'"

es.L: {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “El Señor tiene necesidad de él, y enseguida lo envía de vuelta acá”».
es.B: {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “El Señor lo necesita, y lo devolverá aquí sin demora”».
es.R: Entonces {{plural_you:contéstenle|contestadle}}: “El Señor lo necesita. Pronto lo mandará de vuelta aquí”».

sw.L: semeni, 'Bwana ana haja naye, na papo hapo anamtuma tena hapa.'"
sw.B: waambieni, 'Bwana anamhitaji, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atamrudisha hapa bila kukawia.'"
sw.R: Basi waambieni, 'Bwana anamhitaji. Atamrudisha hapa upesi.'"

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, speaking of himself
decisions.reason: The small word after "the Lord" can go with "Lord" (its master) or with "need" (needs it). Read as "the Lord needs it", the title points to Jesus, who sends for the animal. Some take the owner, or God, as the one meant. The owner is not mentioned, and the bystanders accept the answer.

decisions.choice: and he will send it back here: part of the message, a promise to return the colt
alternatives: Jesus' prediction that the owner will send it at once
decisions.reason: The word "back" (or "again") shows that the animal will be returned. The words are part of what the disciples are to say. Without that word, as in some manuscripts, the sentence could mean the owner will let it go at once.

decisions.choice: sends: a present tense with future sense
decisions.reason: The present is used of what will surely happen.

decisions.choice: without delay
decisions.reason: Balanced varies Mark's frequent "immediately"; Literal keeps it.

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθον καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου, καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they went away and found a colt having been tied at a door outside on the street, and they untie it.

en.L: And they went away and found a colt tied at a door outside on the street, and they untie it.
en.B: They went off and found a colt tied by a doorway, out in the street, and they untied it.
en.R: The two disciples left. They found a young donkey tied outside by a door, out on the street. They untied it.

es.L: Y se fueron y encontraron un pollino atado junto a una puerta, afuera, en la calle, y lo desatan.
es.B: Ellos fueron y encontraron un pollino atado junto a una puerta, afuera en la calle, y lo desataron.
es.R: Los dos discípulos se fueron. Encontraron un burrito atado junto a una puerta, afuera, en la calle. Lo desataron.

sw.L: Na wakaondoka, wakamkuta mwana-punda amefungwa kwenye mlango, nje, barabarani, na wanamfungua.
sw.B: Walikwenda, wakamkuta mwana-punda amefungwa karibu na mlango, nje mtaani, wakamfungua.
sw.R: Wale wanafunzi wawili waliondoka. Walimkuta punda mchanga amefungwa nje karibu na mlango, kando ya barabara. Wakamfungua.

decisions.choice: street: an open lane or way that runs around a block of houses
decisions.reason: The word is used of a street or the way between houses. The colt stood outside, in plain view.

decisions.choice: they untie: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark again tells a past event in the present tense; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: they found: everything happens as Jesus said
decisions.reason: Mark tells it in Jesus' own words (11:2), showing that his instructions were exact.

decisions.choice: The two disciples
decisions.reason: Readable names who went.

decisions.choice: pollino (L, B); burrito (R)
decisions.reason: The animal is a young donkey (meaning decision m4). "Pollino" is the traditional word for a donkey's colt, as in Matthew 21; Readable says "burrito", as the English Readable says "young donkey". "Potro" would suggest a horse.

decisions.choice: mwana-punda (L, B); punda mchanga (R)
decisions.reason: The animal is a young donkey (meaning decision m4). "Mwana-punda" is the word used in Matthew 21; Readable says "punda mchanga" (a young donkey), as the English Readable does.

source.text: καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς· Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον;

records.literal_gloss: And some of those there standing were saying to them, What are you doing untying the colt?

en.L: And some of those standing there were saying to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
en.B: Some of the people standing nearby asked them, "What do you mean by untying that colt?"
en.R: Some people standing there asked them, "Why are you untying that donkey?"

es.L: Y algunos de los que estaban allí de pie les decían: «¿Qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} desatando el pollino?».
es.B: Algunos de los que estaban por allí les preguntaron: «¿Qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} desatando ese pollino?».
es.R: Algunas personas que estaban allí les preguntaron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} ese burrito?».

sw.L: Na baadhi ya wale waliosimama huko walikuwa wakiwaambia, "Mnafanya nini mkimfungua mwana-punda?"
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa wamesimama karibu waliwauliza, "Mnamfungua mwana-punda huyo kwa nini?"
sw.R: Watu fulani waliokuwa wamesimama pale waliwauliza, "Kwa nini mnamfungua punda huyo?"

decisions.choice: were saying: the bystanders challenge them, as Jesus said someone would
decisions.reason: Mark calls them only some of those standing there. Luke 19:33 says the owners spoke; Mark does not say who they were.

decisions.choice: what are you doing: a demand to know why
decisions.reason: The question is a challenge: what right do you have to untie it?

decisions.choice: Why
decisions.reason: Readable puts the challenge as a plain question.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke to them just as said Jesus, and they let go them.

en.L: And they spoke to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them [go].
en.B: The disciples answered as Jesus had told them, and the people let them go.
en.R: The disciples gave the answer Jesus had told them to give. Then the people let them take the donkey.

es.L: Y ellos les hablaron tal como había dicho Jesús, y los dejaron [ir].
es.B: Los discípulos les respondieron como Jesús les había indicado, y la gente los dejó ir.
es.R: Los discípulos respondieron lo que Jesús les había dicho. Entonces la gente los dejó llevarse el burrito.

sw.L: Nao wakawaambia kama Yesu alivyosema, nao wakawaacha [waende].
sw.B: Wanafunzi waliwajibu kama Yesu alivyowaelekeza, na watu wale wakawaruhusu waende.
sw.R: Wanafunzi waliwapa jibu lile ambalo Yesu aliwaambia watoe. Ndipo watu wale wakawaruhusu wamchukue punda.

decisions.choice: just as Jesus had said: the disciples use his words
alternatives: they explained in their own words
decisions.reason: They repeat the answer of 11:3, and it is enough.

decisions.choice: let them go: allowed them, let them take the colt
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or permit. The bystanders let the disciples go with the animal.

decisions.choice: The disciples; the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups, since both are "they" in the Greek.

source.text: καὶ φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw on it the cloaks of them, and he sat on it.

en.L: And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw their cloaks on it, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on it.
en.B: They brought the colt to Jesus and laid their cloaks over its back, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on it.
en.R: They brought the young donkey to Jesus. They put their coats on its back, and Jesus sat on it.

es.L: Y traen el pollino a Jesús y echan sobre él sus mantos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se sentó encima.
es.B: Llevaron el pollino a Jesús y le pusieron encima sus mantos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se sentó sobre el animal.
es.R: Llevaron el burrito a Jesús. Pusieron sus mantos sobre el lomo del animal, y Jesús se sentó encima.

sw.L: Na wanamleta mwana-punda kwa Yesu, na wanamtupia mavazi yao juu yake, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaketi juu yake.
sw.B: Walimletea Yesu mwana-punda, wakaweka mavazi yao mgongoni mwake, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akampanda.
sw.R: Walimletea Yesu yule punda mchanga. Wakaweka makoti yao mgongoni mwake, na Yesu akaketi juu yake.

decisions.choice: he sat on it: the king of Zechariah 9:9
decisions.reason: Jesus had walked all the way from Galilee. Here he rides, as Zechariah 9:9 says Zion's king comes, humble and riding on a donkey's colt. Mark does not quote the verse but tells the scene in its terms.

decisions.choice: cloaks: the outer garment, here used as a saddle
decisions.reason: The cloak was a large outer garment that also served as a blanket. Laid on the animal's back, it made a seat.

decisions.choice: bring, throw: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark again uses the present for vividness; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for an outer garment.

source.text: καὶ πολλοὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And many the cloaks of them spread on the road, and others leafy branches having cut from the fields.

en.L: And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others [spread] leafy branches, having cut [them] from the fields.
en.B: Many people spread their cloaks on the road, and others spread leafy branches they had cut in the fields.
en.R: Many people spread their coats on the road in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Others cut leafy branches in the fields and spread them on the road.

es.L: Y muchos tendieron sus mantos en el camino, y otros, [tendieron] ramas frondosas cortadas de los campos.
es.B: Mucha gente tendió sus mantos sobre el camino, y otros tendieron ramas frondosas que habían cortado en el campo.
es.R: Mucha gente puso sus mantos en el camino, delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Otros cortaron ramas con hojas en el campo y las pusieron en el camino.

sw.L: Na wengi walitandika mavazi yao njiani, na wengine [walitandika] matawi yenye majani, wakiwa wameyakata mashambani.
sw.B: Watu wengi walitandaza mavazi yao barabarani, na wengine wakatandaza matawi yenye majani waliyokuwa wameyakata mashambani.
sw.R: Watu wengi walitandika makoti yao barabarani mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Wengine walikata matawi yenye majani mashambani, wakayatandika barabarani.

decisions.choice: spreading cloaks on the road: a welcome for a king
alternatives: a way to keep the dust down
decisions.reason: When Jehu was proclaimed king, the people spread their cloaks under him (2 Kings 9:13). The crowd honors Jesus as a coming king.

decisions.choice: leafy branches: greenery or leaves cut to lay on the road
decisions.reason: The word means a bed or layer of leaves and rushes. John 12:13 speaks of palm branches; Mark's word is more general.

decisions.choice: others leafy branches: the verb spread is understood
decisions.reason: The verb is not repeated, but the branches too were laid on the road.

decisions.choice: in front of him; spread them on the road
decisions.reason: Readable says where the coats were spread and repeats the verb for the branches.

source.text: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον· Ὡσαννά· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου·

records.literal_gloss: And those going before and those following were crying out, Hosanna; blessed [is] the [one] coming in [the] name of [the] Lord;

en.L: And those going ahead and those following were crying out, "Hosanna! Blessed [is] the one who comes in [the] name of [the] Lord!
en.B: The people walking in front and those coming behind kept shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord's name!
en.R: There were people walking ahead of Jesus and people following behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They all kept shouting, "Hosanna! May God bless the one who comes, sent by the Lord!

es.L: Y los que iban delante y los que seguían gritaban: «¡Hosanna! ¡Bendito el que viene en [el] nombre [del] Señor!
es.B: Los que iban delante y los que venían detrás gritaban una y otra vez: «¡Hosanna! ¡Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor!
es.R: Había gente que caminaba delante de Jesús y gente que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía detrás. Todos gritaban sin parar: «¡Hosanna! ¡Que Dios bendiga al que viene enviado por el Señor!

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa wakienda mbele na wale waliokuwa wakifuata nyuma walikuwa wakipaza sauti, "Hosana! Amebarikiwa yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana!
sw.B: Watu waliotembea mbele na wale waliofuata nyuma walikuwa wakipaza sauti bila kukoma, "Hosana! Amebarikiwa yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana!
sw.R: Kulikuwa na watu waliotembea mbele ya Yesu, na watu waliomfuata nyuma. Wote waliendelea kupaza sauti, "Hosana! Mungu ambariki yeye anayekuja, aliyetumwa na Bwana!

decisions.choice: Hosanna: a Hebrew cry meaning "save, please!", which had become a shout of praise and welcome
decisions.reason: The word comes from Psalm 118:25, "save us, we pray". Sung at festivals, it had become a cry of joy and acclaim. Here it may keep some of its old sense, a plea for God to save, as well as praise.

decisions.choice: Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26
decisions.reason: Psalm 118 was sung by pilgrims at the great festivals. Where the Greek has "Lord", the Hebrew psalm has the divine name. The crowd applies the psalm's welcome to Jesus.

decisions.choice: in the name of the Lord: sent by the Lord, with his authority
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to come as their representative. The one who comes is sent by God.

decisions.choice: were crying out: they shouted again and again
decisions.reason: The tense pictures continued shouting as the procession moved along.

decisions.choice: Hosanna
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word the crowd used, as it is kept in worship. Its sense is given in a footnote.

decisions.choice: people walking ahead of Jesus and people following behind him; May God bless; sent by the Lord
alternatives: those going ahead and those following; Blessed
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the people walked ahead of, makes "blessed" a wish addressed to God, and gives the sense of "in the name of the Lord".

decisions.choice: ¡Hosanna! at every level; el Señor
decisions.reason: As in English and at Matthew 21:9: the cry keeps its own word (meaning decision m1). In Psalm 118:26 "Lord" stands for God's own name (meaning decision m2); Spanish Bibles use "el Señor" for it.

decisions.choice: Hosana at every level; Bwana
decisions.reason: As at Matthew 21:9: "Hosana" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "Hosanna" (meaning decision m1). "Bwana" here stands for God, as in Psalm 118 (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυίδ· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [is] the coming kingdom of the father of us David; Hosanna in the highest.

en.L: Blessed [is] the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"
en.B: Blessed be the kingdom of our father David, now coming! Hosanna in highest heaven!"
en.R: May God bless the kingdom of our ancestor David, which is coming! Hosanna to God in the highest heaven!"

es.L: ¡Bendito el reino venidero de nuestro padre David! ¡Hosanna en las alturas!».
es.B: ¡Bendito el reino de nuestro padre David, que ya llega! ¡Hosanna en lo más alto del cielo!».
es.R: ¡Que Dios bendiga el reino de nuestro antepasado David, que ya viene! ¡Hosanna a Dios en lo más alto del cielo!».

sw.L: Umebarikiwa ufalme unaokuja wa baba yetu Daudi! Hosana katika [mbingu] zilizo juu kabisa!"
sw.B: Ubarikiwe ufalme wa baba yetu Daudi, unaokuja sasa! Hosana juu kabisa mbinguni!"
sw.R: Mungu aubariki ufalme wa babu yetu Daudi, unaokuja! Hosana kwa Mungu aliye juu kabisa mbinguni!"

decisions.choice: the coming kingdom of David: the crowd hopes that God's promise to David's line is about to be fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). These words are not in Psalm 118. Blind Bartimaeus has just called Jesus "Son of David" (10:47-48), and the crowd now welcomes David's kingdom.

decisions.choice: our father David: David as forefather of the nation
decisions.reason: "Father" is used of a forefather. Israel looked back to David as the founder of its royal line.

decisions.choice: Hosanna in the highest: let the cry be raised in the highest heavens, to God himself
decisions.reason: "The highest" means the heights of heaven, where God is (Psalm 148:1). The crowd calls on God in heaven to hear and act.

decisions.choice: the highest heaven (B, R); to God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the highest" refers to. Readable also says "ancestor" for "father".

decisions.choice: el reino venidero
alternatives: el reino que viene de nuestro padre David
decisions.reason: "El reino que viene de nuestro padre David" could be read as a kingdom that comes from David; "venidero" keeps the Greek order and says only that the kingdom is coming (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: babu yetu Daudi (our ancestor David)
decisions.reason: David is the forefather of the nation (meaning decision m2). Readable says "babu", which in Swahili also means an ancestor, as the English Readable says "ancestor"; Literal and Balanced keep "baba yetu".

source.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: And he entered into Jerusalem into the temple, and having looked around at all things, late already being the hour, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into Jerusalem, into the temple, and having looked around at everything, since the hour was already late, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to Bethany with the twelve.
en.B: Jesus went into Jerusalem and into the temple courts. He looked all around at everything, but because it was already late in the day, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left for Bethany with the Twelve.
en.R: Jesus went into Jerusalem and into the temple area. He looked around at everything. But it was already late, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Bethany with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples.

es.L: Y entró en Jerusalén, en el templo; y habiendo mirado todo alrededor, siendo ya avanzada la hora, salió hacia Betania con los doce.
es.B: Jesús entró en Jerusalén y fue a los atrios del templo. Lo observó todo a su alrededor, pero como ya era tarde, salió hacia Betania con los Doce.
es.R: Jesús entró en Jerusalén y fue al área del templo. Miró todo lo que había allí. Pero ya era tarde, así que volvió a Betania con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos.

sw.L: Na aliingia Yerusalemu, ndani ya hekalu; na baada ya kuangalia kila kitu kote kote, kwa kuwa saa ilikuwa tayari imechelewa, alitoka kwenda Bethania pamoja na wale kumi na wawili.
sw.B: Yesu aliingia Yerusalemu, akaenda katika nyua za hekalu. Akaangalia kila kitu kilichokuwa pale, lakini kwa kuwa siku ilikuwa imekwisha kwenda, akaondoka kwenda Bethania pamoja na wale Kumi na Wawili.
sw.R: Yesu aliingia Yerusalemu, akaenda katika eneo la hekalu. Akaangalia kila kitu kilichokuwa pale. Lakini ilikuwa tayari jioni, kwa hiyo akarudi Bethania pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili.

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: The word used here covers the large walled area with its courts and porches. The sanctuary itself, which only priests entered, is called by another word (15:38).

decisions.choice: having looked around at everything: Jesus takes in what is happening there
decisions.reason: He looks, then leaves. What he saw comes to light the next day (11:15-17).

decisions.choice: he went out to Bethany: he lodged outside the city
decisions.reason: At the festivals Jerusalem was crowded with pilgrims, and many stayed in nearby villages. Jesus returns to the city each day (11:15, 11:27).

decisions.choice: the Twelve (B); his twelve disciples (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the number as Mark gives it. Balanced writes it as the name of the group; Readable says who they were.

source.text: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.

records.literal_gloss: And on the next day, having gone out they from Bethany, he was hungry.

en.L: And on the next day, when they had gone out from Bethany, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.B: The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
en.R: The next day, as they left Bethany, Jesus became hungry.

es.L: Y al día siguiente, cuando salieron de Betania, tuvo hambre.
es.B: Al día siguiente, cuando salían de Betania, Jesús tuvo hambre.
es.R: Al día siguiente, mientras salían de Betania, a Jesús le dio hambre.

sw.L: Na siku iliyofuata, walipokwisha kutoka Bethania, alishikwa na njaa.
sw.B: Kesho yake, walipokuwa wakiondoka Bethania, Yesu alihisi njaa.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata, walipokuwa wakitoka Bethania, Yesu aliona njaa.

decisions.choice: having gone out from Bethany: they were on the road back to Jerusalem
alternatives: they had already reached the city
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the scene: on the way from Bethany to the city.

decisions.choice: he was hungry: Jesus' real human need
alternatives: a pretense to teach a lesson
decisions.reason: Mark speaks plainly of Jesus' hunger. What follows becomes a sign, but it begins with an ordinary need.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα τι εὑρήσει ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα, ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν σύκων.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen a fig tree from afar having leaves, he went if perhaps anything he will find on it, and having come to it nothing he found except leaves; for the season not was of figs.

en.L: And seeing from a distance a fig tree having leaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went [to see] if perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would find anything on it, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing except leaves, for it was not [the] season of figs.
en.B: Seeing at a distance a fig tree covered in leaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went over to find out whether there was anything on it. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reached it, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing but leaves, because it was not the time of year for figs.
en.R: In the distance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a fig tree with leaves on it. He went to see if it had any fruit. But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found only leaves. It was not the season for figs.

es.L: Y al ver desde lejos una higuera con hojas, fue [a ver] si acaso encontraría algo en ella, y llegando a ella no encontró nada excepto hojas, pues no era [la] estación de los higos.
es.B: Vio a lo lejos una higuera cubierta de hojas y se acercó para ver si tenía algo. Pero cuando llegó, solo encontró hojas, porque no era la época de los higos.
es.R: A lo lejos vio una higuera con hojas. Fue a ver si tenía algún fruto. Pero cuando llegó, solo encontró hojas. No era la temporada de los higos.

sw.L: Na akiuona mtini kwa mbali ukiwa na majani, alienda [kuona] ikiwa huenda angeona kitu chochote juu yake; na alipoufikia hakukuta chochote isipokuwa majani, kwa sababu haukuwa msimu wa tini.
sw.B: Aliona kwa mbali mtini uliojaa majani, akaukaribia ili aone kama ulikuwa na chochote. Alipoufikia, hakukuta kitu isipokuwa majani, kwa sababu haukuwa msimu wa tini.
sw.R: Kwa mbali aliona mtini wenye majani. Akaenda kuangalia kama ulikuwa na matunda yoyote. Lakini alipofika, alikuta majani tu. Haukuwa msimu wa tini.

decisions.choice: it was not the season for figs: Passover came in spring, and figs ripen in summer
alternatives: the figs had already been picked
decisions.reason: The main fig harvest came in late summer. In spring a fig tree puts out small early fruit with its leaves, so leaves might suggest there was something to eat. This tree had leaves but nothing on it.

decisions.choice: for: Mark explains why there were no figs
alternatives: Mark explains why Jesus went to look
decisions.reason: The note answers the reader's question why the tree was bare. It also shows that the curse that follows is more than a complaint about fruit.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: in the prophets a picture of Israel, and of God finding no fruit among his people
decisions.reason: God compares Israel to early figs (Hosea 9:10) and complains of finding no figs on the tree (Jeremiah 8:13; Micah 7:1). Mark places the temple scene between the two halves of this story (11:12-14; 11:20-21), so each explains the other.

decisions.choice: any fruit
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus was looking for.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι.

records.literal_gloss: And answering he said to it, No longer into the age from you no one fruit may eat.

en.L: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to it, "May no one eat fruit from you any longer, forever."
en.B: He told the tree, "Let no one eat fruit from you ever again."
en.R: Jesus said to the tree, "From now on, may no one ever eat your fruit again!"

es.L: Y respondiendo, le dijo: «Que nadie coma ya fruto de ti, para siempre».
es.B: Y le dijo al árbol: «¡Que nadie vuelva a comer jamás fruto de ti!».
es.R: Jesús le dijo al árbol: «¡De ahora en adelante, que nadie coma nunca más de tu fruto!».

sw.L: Na akijibu, akauambia, "Mtu yeyote asile tena tunda kutoka kwako hata milele."
sw.B: Akauambia mti huo, "Mtu yeyote asile tena tunda lako kamwe."
sw.R: Yesu akauambia mti huo, "Tangu sasa, mtu yeyote asile tena matunda yako kamwe!"

decisions.choice: may no one eat: a wish, spoken as a curse
alternatives: a prediction that no one will eat
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for wishes. Peter later calls it a curse (11:21).

decisions.choice: no longer, into the age: never again
alternatives: not for an age, for a long time
decisions.reason: "Into the age" means forever. With "no longer" it makes a strong never again.

decisions.choice: answering: responding to what he found
decisions.reason: No one has spoken. The word introduces Jesus' response to the bare tree.

decisions.choice: the curse is a sign of judgment
decisions.reason: Like the acted signs of the prophets (Jeremiah 19:1-11), the curse on the fruitless tree points to God's judgment, which Jesus goes on to speak of in the temple.

decisions.choice: ever ... again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two phrases into a natural never again.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And were listening the disciples of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were listening.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples heard it.
en.R: His disciples heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say this.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos estaban escuchando.
es.B: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos lo oyeron.
es.R: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oyeron decir esto.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakisikia.
sw.B: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walisikia maneno hayo.
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimsikia akisema hivyo.

decisions.choice: were listening: the disciples heard the words
decisions.reason: The note prepares for 11:20-21, when Peter remembers what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: heard him say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to Jerusalem.

en.L: And they come to Jerusalem.
en.B: Then they came into Jerusalem.
en.R: Then they arrived in Jerusalem.

es.L: Y llegan a Jerusalén.
es.B: Luego llegaron a Jerusalén.
es.R: Después llegaron a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na wanafika Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Kisha walifika Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Baadaye walifika Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: they come: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark again uses the present for vividness; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the step in the story.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered into the temple he began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves he overturned, \v 16 and not he would allow that anyone should carry a vessel through the temple, \v 17 and he was teaching and saying to them, Not has it been written that The house of me a house of prayer will be called for all the nations?

en.L: And entering into the temple, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves, \v 16 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. \v 17 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching and saying to them, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations'?
en.B: He went into the temple courts and began driving out the people who were selling and buying there. He turned over the money changers' tables and the benches of the dove sellers, \v 16 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not let anyone carry goods through the temple courts. \v 17 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them, saying, "Does Scripture not say, 'My house will be known as a house of prayer for all the nations'?
en.R: Jesus went into the temple area. He began to throw out the people who were buying and selling things there. He turned over the tables where people exchanged money. He also turned over the seats of those who sold doves. \v 16 He would not let anyone carry things through the temple courts. \v 17 Then Jesus taught the people. He said, "In the Scriptures God says, 'My house will be called a house where people from every nation can pray.'

es.L: Y entrando en el templo, comenzó a expulsar a los que vendían y a los que compraban en el templo, y derribó las mesas de los cambistas y los asientos de los que vendían las palomas, \v 16 y no dejaba que nadie transportara ningún objeto a través del templo. \v 17 Y enseñaba y les decía: «¿No está escrito que “Mi casa será llamada casa de oración para todas las naciones”?
es.B: Entró en los atrios del templo y comenzó a expulsar a los que vendían y compraban allí. Derribó las mesas de los que cambiaban dinero y los asientos de los vendedores de palomas, \v 16 y no dejaba que nadie pasara por los atrios del templo cargando mercancías. \v 17 Luego se puso a enseñarles: «¿No dice la Escritura: “Mi casa será conocida como casa de oración para todas las naciones”?
es.R: Jesús entró en el área del templo. Comenzó a echar fuera a la gente que compraba y vendía cosas allí. Volcó las mesas donde se cambiaba dinero. También volcó los asientos de los que vendían palomas. \v 16 No dejaba que nadie pasara por los atrios del templo cargando cosas. \v 17 Luego Jesús enseñó a la gente. Les dijo: «En las Escrituras Dios dice: “Mi casa será llamada una casa donde la gente de todas las naciones pueda orar”.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuingia hekaluni, alianza kuwafukuza wale wanaouza na wale wanaonunua ndani ya hekalu, akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wauzaji wa njiwa, \v 16 na hakumwacha mtu yeyote apitishe chombo katikati ya hekalu. \v 17 Naye alikuwa akifundisha, akiwaambia, "Je, haijaandikwa kwamba, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ya maombi kwa mataifa yote'?
sw.B: Aliingia katika nyua za hekalu, akaanza kuwafukuza watu waliokuwa wakiuza na kununua humo. Akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wauzaji wa njiwa, \v 16 wala hakumruhusu mtu yeyote kupitisha bidhaa katika nyua za hekalu. \v 17 Kisha akawafundisha, akisema, "Je, Maandiko hayasemi, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itajulikana kama nyumba ya maombi kwa mataifa yote'?
sw.R: Yesu aliingia katika eneo la hekalu. Akaanza kuwafukuza watu waliokuwa wakinunua na kuuza vitu humo. Akazipindua meza za watu waliokuwa wakibadilisha fedha. Akapindua pia viti vya watu waliokuwa wakiuza njiwa. \v 16 Hakumruhusu mtu yeyote kubeba vitu akipita katika nyua za hekalu. \v 17 Kisha Yesu akawafundisha watu. Akasema, "Katika Maandiko Mungu anasema, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ambamo watu wa mataifa yote wanaweza kuomba.'

decisions.choice: money changers: they exchanged coins for the silver coins accepted at the temple
decisions.reason: Every Jewish man paid a half-shekel to the temple each year (Exodus 30:13). It had to be paid in coins of Tyrian silver, so pilgrims changed their money in the temple courts.

decisions.choice: doves: the offering of the poor
decisions.reason: The law allowed those who could not afford a lamb to offer two doves or pigeons (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8). Sellers supplied pilgrims with animals that would pass inspection.

decisions.choice: vessel: any container or goods
alternatives: the sacred vessels of the temple
decisions.reason: The word is general: a jar, a basket, a load. People used the temple courts as a shortcut, and Jesus stopped them.

decisions.choice: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations: Isaiah 56:7
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:6-7 God promises that foreigners who hold to him will be brought to his holy mountain, and their offerings accepted. The trading likely took place in the outer court, the only part of the temple open to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: began to cast out: the same verb Mark uses for driving out demons
decisions.reason: The verb is a forceful one. Mark uses it for casting out demons (1:34, 3:15).

decisions.choice: driving out (B); throw out (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word used for demons; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for forcing people out.

decisions.choice: In the Scriptures God says
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement and says who speaks in Isaiah: the "my house" is God's.

decisions.choice: expulsar (L, B); echar fuera (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Mark uses for driving out demons (meaning decision m5). "Expulsar" and "echar fuera" are the words used for that elsewhere in Spanish, so the force of the act comes through; "sacar" would be too mild.

decisions.choice: Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, with a span
alternatives: yangu with no span, as the English
decisions.reason: The English "My" opens the quotation and is capitalised anyway, so it has no span. Swahili puts the possessive after the noun, where it can take the setting; here it is God who speaks, through Isaiah. As at Matthew 21:13.

decisions.choice: nyumba ya maombi
decisions.reason: "Maombi" (prayer, asking) is the word used for prayer in Matthew 21:13 and 21:22; "sala" leans towards set prayers. Readable says "kuomba", the same root.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

records.literal_gloss: You however have made it a den of robbers.

en.L: But you have made it a den of robbers."
en.B: But you have turned it into a hideout for bandits."
en.R: But you have made it a hiding place for robbers!"

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} cueva de bandidos».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:han convertido|habéis convertido}} en una guarida de bandidos».
es.R: ¡Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:han convertido|habéis convertido}} en un escondite de bandidos!».

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mmeifanya kuwa pango la majambazi."
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza kuwa maficho ya majambazi."
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mmeifanya kuwa mahali pa kujificha majambazi!"

decisions.choice: a den of robbers: Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: In his temple sermon Jeremiah warned people who did wrong and then came to the temple feeling safe. God asked whether his house had become a den of robbers, and warned that he would destroy it as he had destroyed Shiloh (Jeremiah 7:9-14).

decisions.choice: robbers: bandits, men of violence
decisions.reason: The word means a bandit or raider, not a dishonest trader. A den is where robbers hide and feel safe after their crimes. The charge is that the temple has become such a refuge, not only that prices were unfair.

decisions.choice: you: stated, in contrast with God's purpose
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: God said one thing; you have made it another.

decisions.choice: a hideout for bandits
decisions.reason: Balanced uses plain words for Jeremiah's picture. Literal keeps the familiar phrase.

decisions.choice: bandidos
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit, not a sneak thief (meaning decision m2); Jeremiah's picture is of a den where such men hide. "Ladrones" usually means thieves. As at Matthew 21:13.

decisions.choice: majambazi
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit (meaning decision m2); "jambazi" is exactly that, where "mwizi" is a thief. As at Matthew 21:13.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And heard the chief priests and the scribes, and they were seeking how him they might destroy; they were afraid for of him, for all the crowd was astonished at the teaching of him.

en.L: And the chief priests and the scribes heard [it], and they were seeking how they might destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; for they were afraid of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for the whole crowd was astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.
en.B: When the chief priests and the scribes heard about this, they began looking for a way to do away with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They feared {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since the whole crowd was spellbound by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law heard about this. They started looking for a way to kill Jesus. They were afraid of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because all the people were amazed at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught.

es.L: Y [lo] oyeron los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas, y buscaban cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} destruirían; porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} temían, pues toda la multitud estaba asombrada de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas se enteraron, y comenzaron a buscar la manera de acabar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Pues {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} temían, ya que toda la multitud estaba maravillada con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley se enteraron de esto. Empezaron a buscar la manera de matar a Jesús. Pero {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenían miedo, porque toda la gente estaba asombrada de lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enseñaba.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walisikia [hayo], nao walikuwa wakitafuta namna ya kumwangamiza; kwa kuwa walikuwa wakimwogopa, maana umati wote ulikuwa ukishangazwa na mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi waliposikia habari hiyo, walianza kutafuta njia ya kumwangamiza. Walikuwa wakimwogopa, kwa sababu umati wote ulivutiwa sana na mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walisikia habari hiyo. Wakaanza kutafuta njia ya kumuua Yesu. Walikuwa wakimwogopa, kwa sababu watu wote walishangaa sana kwa mambo aliyofundisha.

decisions.choice: chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families who ran the temple
decisions.reason: The chief priests controlled the temple and its trade. Jesus had said they would reject him (8:31; 10:33).

decisions.choice: destroy: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb is used of killing, as in 3:6.

decisions.choice: for ... for: they feared him because the crowd was with him
decisions.reason: The two explanations follow each other: they wanted to kill him but feared him, and they feared him because the crowd hung on his words.

decisions.choice: the leading priests; the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain descriptions, as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter; they return in 11:27. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter; they return in 11:27. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.

records.literal_gloss: And when late it became, they were going out of the city.

en.L: And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
en.B: And each evening they went out of the city.
en.R: Every evening Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples left the city.

es.L: Y cuando se hacía tarde, salían fuera de la ciudad.
es.B: Y cada tarde salían de la ciudad.
es.R: Cada tarde, Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos salían de la ciudad.

sw.L: Na kila ilipokuwa jioni, walikuwa wakitoka nje ya mji.
sw.B: Na kila jioni walitoka nje ya mji.
sw.R: Kila jioni Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walitoka nje ya mji.

decisions.choice: whenever evening came, they would go out: something done each day
decisions.reason: The word for "whenever" with a past tense of repeated action usually describes a habit. It may also mean simply that evening came that day.

decisions.choice: they went out
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have "he went out", speaking of Jesus alone. The SBLGNT reads "they", which includes the disciples, who are with him the next morning (11:20). Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who went out.

source.text: Καὶ παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And passing by in the morning they saw the fig tree having been dried up from [the] roots.

en.L: And passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from [the] roots.
en.B: Early the next day, as they went along, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots up.
en.R: The next morning, as they walked past, they saw the fig tree. It had dried up completely, all the way down to its roots.

es.L: Y al pasar de madrugada, vieron la higuera secada desde [las] raíces.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, al pasar por allí, vieron que la higuera se había secado de raíz.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, cuando pasaban por allí, vieron la higuera. Se había secado por completo, hasta las raíces.

sw.L: Na wakipita asubuhi, waliuona mtini ukiwa umenyauka tangu mizizi.
sw.B: Asubuhi iliyofuata, walipokuwa wakipita, waliuona mtini ule umekauka kabisa tangu mizizi yake.
sw.R: Asubuhi iliyofuata, walipokuwa wakipita pale, waliuona ule mtini. Ulikuwa umekauka kabisa, hadi kwenye mizizi yake.

decisions.choice: withered: dried up, dead
decisions.reason: The word is used of plants that dry up and die (4:6).

decisions.choice: from the roots: completely, past any recovery
decisions.reason: A tree dried from its roots will not grow again (Job 18:16; Hosea 9:16).

decisions.choice: passing by in the morning: the next morning, on the same road
decisions.reason: They pass the tree again on their way into the city (11:12, 11:19).

decisions.choice: the next day (B); the next morning (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which morning is meant.

source.text: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.

records.literal_gloss: And having remembered Peter says to him, Rabbi, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.

en.L: And Peter, remembering, says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cursed has withered."
en.B: Peter remembered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, Rabbi! The fig tree {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cursed is all dried up."
en.R: Peter remembered what Jesus had said. He said, "Teacher, look! The fig tree {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put a curse on has dried up!"

es.L: Y acordándose, Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Rabí, mira, la higuera que maldijiste se ha secado».
es.B: Pedro se acordó y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Mira, Rabí! La higuera que maldijiste se ha secado por completo».
es.R: Pedro se acordó de lo que Jesús había dicho. Le dijo: «¡Maestro, mira! ¡La higuera a la que echaste una maldición se ha secado!».

sw.L: Na Petro, akiwa amekumbuka, anamwambia, "Rabi, angalia! Mtini ule uliouapiza umekauka."
sw.B: Petro alikumbuka, akamwambia, "Tazama, Rabi! Mtini uliouapiza umekauka kabisa."
sw.R: Petro alikumbuka maneno ya Yesu. Akasema, "Mwalimu, tazama! Mtini ule ulioulaani umekauka!"

decisions.choice: cursed: called down harm on it
decisions.reason: Peter names Jesus' words of 11:14 a curse, a word spoken against something that brings about harm.

decisions.choice: has withered: a perfect, it dried up and stays dead
alternatives: is in the process of withering
decisions.reason: The tense describes a finished event with lasting result.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a Hebrew title of respect for a teacher
decisions.reason: As at 9:5, Peter uses the title for teachers of the law.

decisions.choice: Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the Hebrew title, as in earlier chapters. It also says what Peter remembered.

decisions.choice: Rabí (L, B); Maestro (R)
decisions.reason: As in John: "Rabí" keeps the Hebrew title of respect (meaning decision m3), and Readable says what it means, as the English Readable says "Teacher".

decisions.choice: Rabi (L, B); Mwalimu (R)
decisions.reason: As in John: "Rabi" keeps the Hebrew title of respect (meaning decision m3), and Readable says what it means, as the English Readable says "Teacher".

decisions.choice: uliouapiza (L, B); ulioulaani (R)
decisions.reason: Both verbs mean to call down harm on something (meaning decision m1). "Kuapiza" is the plain word for cursing a thing or person; Readable uses "kulaani", the more widely known word.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus says to them, Have faith of God.

en.L: And Jesus, answering, says to them, "Have faith in God.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Have faith in God.
en.R: Jesus answered, "You must have faith in God.

es.L: Y respondiendo Jesús, les dice: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} fe en Dios.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} fe en Dios.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «{{plural_you:Deben|Debéis}} tener fe en Dios.

sw.L: Na Yesu, akijibu, anawaambia, "Mwe na imani kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Mwe na imani kwa Mungu.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Ni lazima mwe na imani kwa Mungu.

decisions.choice: faith in God: God is the one trusted
alternatives: the kind of faith God gives
decisions.reason: The Greek says "faith of God". This form can name the one in whom faith is placed, as in "faith of Jesus Christ" in Paul. The sayings that follow speak of the one who believes and does not doubt (11:23-24), so faith directed to God is meant.

decisions.choice: have: a command
decisions.reason: The same form can state a fact (you have faith in God) or give a command. Jesus' answer to Peter is most likely a call to trust God.

decisions.choice: Have faith in God
alternatives: If you have faith in God
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts begin with "if", making the saying the start of a condition: if you have faith in God, then whoever says to this mountain ... (compare Matthew 21:21; Luke 17:6). The SBLGNT has the command without "if". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: answering: responding to what Peter had said
decisions.reason: Peter had not asked a question; Jesus responds to his remark.

decisions.choice: faith
decisions.reason: Faith is a key term and keeps the same word at every level.

decisions.choice: You must
decisions.reason: Readable makes the command plain.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ πιστεύῃ ὅτι ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται, ἔσται αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you that whoever says to the mountain this, Be taken up and be thrown into the sea, and not doubts in the heart of him but believes that what he says happens, it will be for him.

en.L: Truly I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, 'Be taken up and thrown into the sea,' and does not doubt in {{gender:their|his}} heart but believes that what {{gender:they say|he says}} happens, it will be [done] for {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Truly I tell you, if anyone tells this mountain, 'Rise up and be hurled into the sea,' and does not waver in their heart, but believes that what they say is taking place, it will be done for them.
en.R: I tell you the truth: Suppose someone tells this mountain, 'Be picked up and thrown into the sea!' They must not doubt in their heart. They must believe that what they say is going to happen. Then it will happen for them.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que cualquiera que diga a este monte: “Sé levantado y arrojado al mar”, y no dude en su corazón, sino que crea que lo que dice sucede, le será [hecho].
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si alguien le dice a este monte: “Sé arrancado de aquí y arrojado al mar”, y no vacila en su corazón, sino que cree que lo que dice está sucediendo, así se le hará.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: supongamos que alguien le dice a este monte: “¡Sé levantado y arrojado al mar!”. Esa persona no debe dudar en su corazón. Debe creer que lo que dice va a suceder. Entonces se le cumplirá.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia kwamba yeyote atakayeuambia mlima huu, 'Uinuliwe na utupwe baharini,' wala asiwe na shaka moyoni mwake, bali aamini kwamba anachosema kinatokea, itakuwa [hivyo] kwake.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, mtu yeyote akiuambia mlima huu, 'Uinuliwe na kutupwa baharini,' bila kusitasita moyoni mwake, bali akiamini kwamba anachosema kinatendeka, atafanyiwa hivyo.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Tuseme mtu anauambia mlima huu, 'Uinuliwe na kutupwa baharini!' Asiwe na shaka moyoni mwake. Aamini kwamba anachosema kitatokea. Ndipo kitatokea kwa ajili yake.

decisions.choice: moving a mountain into the sea: doing what seems impossible
alternatives: a promise to move actual mountains on request
decisions.reason: Removing mountains was a picture of overcoming the impossible (Zechariah 4:7; 1 Corinthians 13:2).

decisions.choice: this mountain: the Mount of Olives they were crossing, or the temple mount ahead of them
decisions.reason: They were on the road over the Mount of Olives, which Zechariah 14:4 says will be split. Some see the temple mount, under judgment in this chapter. "This" points to a mountain in view; Mark does not say which.

decisions.choice: doubt: be divided in mind, waver between two views
decisions.reason: The verb pictures someone torn between trust and distrust. Its opposite here is to believe.

decisions.choice: happens: a present tense, as good as already happening
decisions.reason: Faith counts what is said as already coming to pass.

decisions.choice: anyone ... their, they, them
decisions.reason: The saying applies to anyone, so Balanced and Readable use inclusive pronouns. Literal follows the Greek with a gender setting.

decisions.choice: They must not doubt ... They must believe
alternatives: and does not doubt but believes
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long condition into short sentences.

decisions.choice: En verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of the single "amen" used throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter, as in Matthew.

decisions.choice: no gender span (su corazón, lo que dice, se le hará)
alternatives: a gender span, as the English has
decisions.reason: The English needs "their" or "his" for the one who speaks (English decision r-en-1). Spanish "su", "dice" and "le" say nothing about the person's sex, so there is no second wording for the setting to offer.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of the single "amen" used throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter, as in Matthew.

decisions.choice: Uinuliwe na kutupwa (be lifted and thrown), passive
decisions.reason: The Greek verbs are passive, as at Matthew 21:21. An active command would make the mountain move itself, so the passive is kept at every level, as the English Literal and Readable keep it.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε, πιστεύετε ὅτι ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this I say to you, all things whatever you pray and ask, believe that you received, and it will be to you.

en.L: For this reason I say to you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you received [them], and [they] will be yours.
en.B: So I tell you: everything you request when you pray, believe that you received it, and you will have it.
en.R: So I tell you this: When you pray and ask God for things, believe that you have already received them. Then they will be yours.

es.L: Por esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: todo cuanto {{plural_you:oran|oráis}} y {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} que lo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, y lo {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}}.
es.B: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: todo lo que {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en oración, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} que ya lo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, y lo {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}}.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}} y le {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} cosas a Dios, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} que ya las {{plural_you:han recibido|habéis recibido}}. Entonces {{plural_you:serán de ustedes|serán vuestras}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii nawaambia, vitu vyote mnavyoviombea katika sala na kuviomba, aminini kwamba mlivipokea, na vitakuwa vyenu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nawaambia: chochote mnachoomba mnaposali, aminini kwamba mmekwisha kukipokea, nanyi mtakuwa nacho.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nawaambia hivi: Mnaposali na kumwomba Mungu vitu, aminini kwamba mmekwisha kuvipokea. Ndipo vitakuwa vyenu.

decisions.choice: received: a past tense, the answer counted as already given
decisions.reason: Jesus tells them to believe they have received it, though it is not yet in hand.

decisions.choice: you received
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts change the past tense to a present or future, which reads more smoothly. The SBLGNT has the past tense. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: pray and ask: asking in prayer
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe one act from two sides: prayer that asks God for something.

decisions.choice: because of this: the promise rests on faith in God (11:22)
alternatives: a technique for getting anything one wants
decisions.reason: The saying grows out of "have faith in God" and is followed at once by the command to forgive (11:25).

decisions.choice: ask God
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the request is made.

source.text: καὶ ὅταν στήκετε προσευχόμενοι, ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And whenever you stand praying, forgive if anything you have against anyone, so that also the Father of you who [is] in the heavens may forgive you the trespasses of you.

en.L: And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who [is] in the heavens may also forgive you your trespasses."
en.B: And whenever you stand up to pray, if you are holding anything against anyone, forgive them, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your wrongdoings as well."
en.R: When you stand and pray, forgive anyone you have something against. Then your Father in heaven will also forgive you for the wrong things you have done."

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} de pie orando, {{plural_you:perdonen|perdonad}}, si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} algo contra alguien, para que también {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}} que [está] en los cielos {{plural_you:les|os}} perdone {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} ofensas».
es.B: Y cuando {{plural_you:se pongan|os pongáis}} de pie para orar, si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} algo contra alguien, {{plural_you:perdónenlo|perdonadlo}}, para que también {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}} que está en el cielo {{plural_you:les|os}} perdone {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} faltas».
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} de pie orando, {{plural_you:perdonen|perdonad}} a cualquier persona contra la que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} algo. Así {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}} que está en el cielo también {{plural_you:les|os}} perdonará el mal que {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} hecho».

sw.L: Na wakati wowote mnaposimama mkiomba, sameheni ikiwa mna kitu dhidi ya mtu, ili pia Baba yenu aliye katika mbingu awasamehe ninyi makosa yenu."
sw.B: Na mnaposimama kusali, kama mna jambo lolote dhidi ya mtu, msameheni, ili Baba yenu aliye mbinguni naye awasamehe makosa yenu."
sw.R: Mnaposimama na kusali, msameheni mtu yeyote mliye na jambo dhidi yake. Ndipo Baba yenu aliye mbinguni atawasamehe ninyi pia mabaya mliyotenda."

decisions.choice: stand praying: standing was a usual posture for prayer
decisions.reason: People commonly stood to pray (1 Samuel 1:26; Luke 18:11-13).

decisions.choice: so that your Father may forgive you: forgiving others and being forgiven belong together
decisions.reason: Those who come to God asking forgiveness must forgive others, as in the prayer Jesus taught (Matthew 6:12, 14-15).

decisions.choice: trespasses: false steps, wrongs done
decisions.reason: The word means a false step or offense, a wrong done against God or others.

decisions.choice: your Father who is in the heavens: God, the Father of those who pray
decisions.reason: The plural "heavens" follows Hebrew idiom. This is the only place in Mark where Jesus says "your Father".

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 26
alternatives: add verse 26: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in the heavens forgive your trespasses
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add these words here. The earliest manuscripts lack them, and they are almost the same as Matthew 6:15, from which scribes likely copied them to round out the saying. Verse 26 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: heaven; wrongdoings (B), wrong things you have done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the usual singular "heaven" and plain words for wrongs. Literal keeps the plural and the older word.

decisions.choice: ofensas (L); faltas (B); el mal que hayan hecho (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a false step, a wrong done (meaning decision m3), not the usual word for sin, so "pecados" is avoided. "Ofensas" and "faltas" are everyday words for wrongs; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: makosa (L, B); mabaya mliyotenda (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a false step, a wrong done (meaning decision m3), not the usual word for sin, so "dhambi" is avoided. "Makosa" is the everyday word for wrongs; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: And they come again to Jerusalem.

en.L: And they come again to Jerusalem.
en.B: They came back into Jerusalem once more.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went back to Jerusalem again.

es.L: Y vienen otra vez a Jerusalén.
es.B: Volvieron una vez más a Jerusalén.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos volvieron otra vez a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na wanakuja tena Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Walirudi tena Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walirudi tena Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: they come: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As before, Mark tells the past in the present; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: again: the third day running that Jesus enters the city
alternatives: a return after a long time
decisions.reason: Jesus came into the city in 11:11 and 11:15, and now again.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who came.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And in the temple walking him come to him the chief priests and the scribes and the elders, \v 28 and they were saying to him, By what authority these things are you doing?

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \v 28 and were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "By what authority are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing these things?
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was walking in the temple courts, the chief priests, the scribes and the elders came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \v 28 and demanded, "What authority do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have for doing these things?
en.R: Jesus was walking in the temple area. The leading priests, the teachers of God's law, and the elders came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 28 They said, "What right do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do these things?

es.L: Y mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} camina por el templo, vienen a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas y los ancianos, \v 28 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «¿Con qué autoridad haces estas cosas?
es.B: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} andaba por los atrios del templo, se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron los jefes de los sacerdotes, los escribas y los ancianos, \v 28 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Con qué autoridad haces estas cosas?
es.R: Jesús caminaba por el área del templo. Los jefes de los sacerdotes, los maestros de la ley y los ancianos se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron. \v 28 Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Qué derecho tienes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} para hacer estas cosas?

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipokuwa akitembea hekaluni, wanamjia wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi na wazee, \v 28 nao walikuwa wakimwambia, "Unafanya mambo haya kwa mamlaka gani?
sw.B: Alipokuwa akitembea katika nyua za hekalu, wakuu wa makuhani, waandishi na wazee walimjia, \v 28 wakamhoji, "Una mamlaka gani ya kufanya mambo haya?
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akitembea katika eneo la hekalu. Wakuu wa makuhani, walimu wa sheria na wazee walimjia. \v 28 Wakamwuliza, "Una ruhusa gani ya kufanya mambo haya?

decisions.choice: the chief priests, the scribes and the elders: the groups that made up the council of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Together they formed the Sanhedrin, the ruling council (14:53, 15:1). Jesus had named these three as those who would reject him (8:31).

decisions.choice: authority: the right to act, given by someone with power to give it
decisions.reason: The word means authority or right. Mark has said that Jesus taught with authority (1:22, 1:27) and has authority to forgive sins (2:10).

decisions.choice: these things: above all the action in the temple, and perhaps his teaching there
decisions.reason: The question comes the day after Jesus drove out the traders. Mark does not limit "these things".

decisions.choice: What right
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for authority. It also says "leading priests" and "teachers of God's law", as before.

decisions.choice: autoridad (L, B); derecho (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the right to act, given by someone with power to give it (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced say "autoridad"; Readable says "derecho", as the English Readable says "right". The same through verse 33.

decisions.choice: ruhusa (permission, right)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "right". Swahili "haki" is kept for righteousness, so Readable says "ruhusa", the right to act that someone gives (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced say "mamlaka". The same through verse 33.

source.text: ἢ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς;

records.literal_gloss: Or who to you gave the authority this that these things you should do?

en.L: Or who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this authority, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} should do these things?"
en.B: Or who is it that gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this authority to do them?"
en.R: Who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the right to do them?"

es.L: ¿O quién {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dio esta autoridad para que hagas estas cosas?».
es.B: ¿O quién {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dio autoridad para hacerlas?».
es.R: ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dio el derecho de hacerlas?».

sw.L: Ama ni nani aliyekupa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} mamlaka haya kwamba ufanye mambo haya?"
sw.B: Au ni nani aliyekupa mamlaka haya ya kuyafanya?"
sw.R: Nani alikupa ruhusa ya kuyafanya?"

decisions.choice: or who gave you: the second question asks for the source
alternatives: a separate question on another subject
decisions.reason: The second question narrows the first: who stands behind you? The leaders had not given him authority, and they did not accept that God had.

decisions.choice: authority: the same word as in the first question
decisions.reason: The repeated word ties the questions together.

decisions.choice: to do them
alternatives: that you should do these things
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid repeating "these things" a third time.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον, καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι, καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, I will ask you one word, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority these things I do.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "I will ask you one question; answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
en.B: Jesus said to them, "I will put one question to you. Answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and then I will tell you what authority I have for doing these things.
en.R: Jesus answered, "Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ask you one question. If you give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} an answer, I will tell you who gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the right to do these things.

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} preguntaré una cosa; {{plural_you:respóndanme|respondedme}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} diré con qué autoridad hago estas cosas.
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a hacer una sola pregunta. {{plural_you:Contéstenme|Contestadme}}, y entonces {{plural_you:les|os}} diré con qué autoridad hago estas cosas.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Déjenme|Dejadme}} {{plural_you:hacerles|haceros}} una pregunta. Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:responden|respondéis}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} diré quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dio el derecho de hacer estas cosas.

sw.L: Naye Yesu akawaambia, "Nitawauliza swali moja; nijibuni, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawaambia ninafanya mambo haya kwa mamlaka gani.
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Nitawauliza swali moja tu. Nijibuni, kisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitawaambia nina mamlaka gani ya kufanya mambo haya.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Niruhusuni niwaulize swali moja. Mkinipa jibu, nitawaambia ni nani aliyenipa ruhusa ya kufanya mambo haya.

decisions.choice: word: here a question or matter
decisions.reason: The noun often means a matter or saying. Here it is the question Jesus is about to ask.

decisions.choice: answering a question with a question: a common form of debate among teachers
decisions.reason: Teachers of the law often replied with a counter-question. Jesus' question bears directly on theirs.

decisions.choice: answer me, and I will tell you: if you answer, I will tell
decisions.reason: A command followed by a promise works as a condition.

decisions.choice: If you give me an answer, I will tell you
alternatives: answer me, and I will tell you
decisions.reason: Readable writes the condition as a plain "if".

decisions.choice: una cosa
decisions.reason: The Greek says "one word", here a question (meaning decision m1). "Una palabra" does not mean a question in Spanish; "una cosa" is the ordinary way to say it and keeps the shape, as at Matthew 21:24.

decisions.choice: swali moja (one question)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "one word", here a question (meaning decision m1). "Neno" can mean a matter, but "swali" says plainly what Jesus will ask, as at Matthew 21:24.

source.text: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;

records.literal_gloss: The baptism of John, from heaven was it or from men?

en.L: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from {{gender:people|men}}?
en.B: John's baptism: did it come from heaven, or from {{gender:human beings|men}}?
en.R: Was John's baptism from God, or was it only from {{gender:people|men}}?

es.L: El bautismo de Juan, ¿era del cielo o de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}?
es.B: El bautismo de Juan, ¿venía del cielo o de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}?
es.R: ¿El bautismo de Juan venía de Dios, o era solo cosa de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}?
