sw.L: Ubatizo ule wa Yohana, ulikuwa wa kutoka mbinguni, au wa kutoka kwa wanadamu?
sw.B: Ubatizo wa Yohana ulikuwa na chanzo gani: mbinguni, au kwa binadamu?
sw.R: Je, ubatizo wa Yohana ulitoka kwa Mungu, au ulitoka kwa watu tu?

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: "Heaven" was a reverent way of speaking of God without naming him.

decisions.choice: the baptism of John: John's whole work of baptizing and the message that went with it
decisions.reason: John called people to be baptized as a sign of repentance (1:4-5) and pointed to the one coming after him (1:7-8). Jesus himself was baptized by John (1:9).

decisions.choice: men: human beings, people in general
decisions.reason: The word is used of humans as opposed to God.

decisions.choice: God; only
decisions.reason: Readable says what "heaven" stands for. "Only" brings out the contrast between a human and a divine source.

decisions.choice: wanadamu (L), binadamu (B), watu (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "people" or "men" here. Swahili "wanadamu", "binadamu" and "watu" already mean human beings of either sex, and "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so there is no second wording for the setting. The same in verse 32.

source.text: ἀποκρίθητέ μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Answer me.

en.L: Answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!"
en.R: Give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} an answer!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Respóndanme|Respondedme}}».
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Respóndanme|Respondedme}}!».
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Denme|Dadme}} una respuesta!».

sw.L: Nijibuni."
sw.B: Nijibuni!"
sw.R: Nipeni jibu!"

decisions.choice: answer me: the command is repeated as a challenge
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the demand of 11:29. The leaders who asked him a question must now answer one.

source.text: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες· Τί εἴπωμεν;

records.literal_gloss: And they were reasoning among themselves saying, What should we say?

en.L: And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "What should we say?
en.B: They talked it over among themselves: "What are we to say?
en.R: They argued about it with each other. They said, "What should we say?

es.L: Y discutían entre sí, diciendo: «¿Qué diremos?
es.B: Ellos lo hablaron entre sí: «¿Qué vamos a decir?
es.R: Ellos discutieron sobre esto entre ellos. Decían: «¿Qué debemos responder?

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakijadiliana wao kwa wao, wakisema, "Tuseme nini?
sw.B: Walishauriana wao kwa wao, "Tuseme nini sasa?
sw.R: Walibishana wao kwa wao kuhusu jambo hilo. Wakasema, "Tuseme nini?

decisions.choice: What should we say?
alternatives: omit the question: they reasoned, saying, If we say ...
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts do not have this short question, and the sentence goes straight on to "If we say". The SBLGNT includes it with a smaller number of manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they were reasoning: they discussed it back and forth
decisions.reason: The tense pictures a discussion that went on for a time.

decisions.choice: argued about it
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for their discussion.

source.text: ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: If we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then not did you believe him?

en.L: If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
en.B: If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reply, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
en.R: If we say, 'God sent him,' Jesus will ask us, 'Then why did you not believe John?'

es.L: Si decimos: “Del cielo”, dirá: “¿Por qué, pues, no le {{plural_you:creyeron|creísteis}}?”.
es.B: Si decimos: “Del cielo”, nos responderá: “Entonces, ¿por qué no le {{plural_you:creyeron|creísteis}}?”.
es.R: Si decimos: “Dios lo envió”, Jesús nos preguntará: “Entonces, ¿por qué no le {{plural_you:creyeron|creísteis}} a Juan?”.

sw.L: Ikiwa tutasema, 'Kutoka mbinguni,' atasema, 'Basi kwa nini hamkumwamini?'
sw.B: Tukisema, 'Ulitoka mbinguni,' atatujibu, 'Basi mbona hamkumwamini?'
sw.R: Tukisema, 'Mungu ndiye aliyemtuma,' Yesu atatuuliza, 'Basi kwa nini hamkumwamini Yohana?'

decisions.choice: believe him: believe John and his message
decisions.reason: "Him" is John. To believe him was to accept his call to repent and his witness to the one coming after him (1:7-8).

decisions.choice: he will say: Jesus
decisions.reason: The leaders expect Jesus to turn their answer against them.

decisions.choice: God sent him; Jesus; John
decisions.reason: Readable says what "from heaven" means and names the two men.

source.text: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ὄχλον, ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάννην ὄντως ὅτι προφήτης ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: But should we say, From men? They were fearing the crowd, for all were holding John really that a prophet he was.

en.L: But should we say, 'From {{gender:people|men}}'?"—they were afraid of the crowd, for all held that John had really been a prophet.
en.B: But suppose we say, 'From {{gender:human beings|men}}' . . ." They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone held that John was truly a prophet.
en.R: But what if we say, 'It came from {{gender:people|men}}'?" They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone was sure that John was a real prophet.

es.L: Pero ¿diremos: “De {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}”?». Temían a la multitud, porque todos tenían a Juan como alguien que en verdad era profeta.
es.B: Pero si decimos: “De {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}”...». Tenían miedo a la multitud, porque todos consideraban que Juan había sido un verdadero profeta.
es.R: Pero ¿y si decimos: “Vino de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}”?». Tenían miedo de la multitud, porque todos estaban seguros de que Juan era un verdadero profeta.

sw.L: Lakini tuseme, 'Kutoka kwa wanadamu'?" Waliuogopa umati, kwa maana wote walimhesabu Yohana kuwa kweli alikuwa nabii.
sw.B: Lakini tukisema, 'Ulitoka kwa binadamu' . . ." Waliuogopa umati wa watu, kwa sababu wote walimchukulia Yohana kuwa nabii kweli.
sw.R: Lakini tukisema, 'Ulitoka kwa watu'?" Waliuogopa umati wa watu, kwa sababu kila mtu alikuwa na hakika kwamba Yohana alikuwa nabii wa kweli.

decisions.choice: But should we say, From men?: the leaders do not finish the thought, and Mark completes it
alternatives: a full sentence: But we say, From men, and they feared the people
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks off. Mark explains why they could not give that answer: they feared the crowd. The words can also be read as a question they leave hanging.

decisions.choice: the crowd held John to be a prophet
decisions.reason: Crowds from all Judea and Jerusalem had gone out to John (1:5). Though Herod had put him to death (6:14-29), the people still honored him as a prophet.

decisions.choice: really: truly, in fact
decisions.reason: The word stresses that the people were convinced.

decisions.choice: the broken-off sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the leaders stop in mid-sentence, before Mark's explanation.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering to Jesus they say, Not we know.

en.L: And answering Jesus, they say, "We do not know."
en.B: So they replied to Jesus, "We do not know."
en.R: So they answered Jesus, "We do not know."

es.L: Y respondiendo a Jesús, dicen: «No sabemos».
es.B: Así que respondieron a Jesús: «No lo sabemos».
es.R: Entonces le contestaron a Jesús: «No lo sabemos».

sw.L: Nao, wakimjibu Yesu, wanasema, "Hatujui."
sw.B: Basi wakamjibu Yesu, "Hatujui."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo walimjibu Yesu, "Hatujui."

decisions.choice: they say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark again uses the present for vividness; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: we do not know: the leaders refuse to judge John's work
decisions.reason: They claim to judge Jesus' authority but will not say whether John was sent by God.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the answer follows from their reasoning.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus says to them, Neither I tell you by what authority these things I do.

en.L: And Jesus says to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Then I am not telling you what authority I have for doing these things, either."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Then I will not tell you who gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the right to do these things."

es.L: Y Jesús les dice: «Tampoco yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo con qué autoridad hago estas cosas».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Entonces yo tampoco {{plural_you:les|os}} digo con qué autoridad hago estas cosas».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Entonces yo tampoco {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a decir quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dio el derecho de hacer estas cosas».

sw.L: Na Yesu anawaambia, "Hata {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} siwaambii ni kwa mamlaka gani ninafanya mambo haya."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Basi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} pia sitawaambia nina mamlaka gani ya kufanya mambo haya."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Basi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} pia sitawaambia ni nani aliyenipa ruhusa ya kufanya mambo haya."

decisions.choice: neither I: Jesus matches their refusal
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" sets his answer beside theirs: since you will not say, I will not say.

decisions.choice: the answer is implied: his authority comes from the same source as John's
decisions.reason: John pointed to Jesus (1:7-8), and Jesus was baptized by John when the voice from heaven spoke (1:9-11). The parable that follows (12:1-12) makes his claim plainer.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the link to their answer clear.
